GOF test for an auxiliary (unmodelled) statistic

Source: R/gof.R
gof_auxiliary.Rd

Implements the auxiliary-statistic test of Boschi & Wit (2025), Section 3.7 / eq. 20. Tests whether a covariate auxiliary that is not part of model has nonetheless been adequately captured indirectly by the fitted model. Uses the simulation-based p-value described in the paper: n_sim replicates of \(G^*[\hat\gamma, u]\) are drawn from i.i.d. standard normals, the test statistic \(T_\phi = \sup_u |G[\hat\gamma, u]|\) is computed, and the empirical p-value is the fraction of replicates with \(T_{\phi,b}^* \ge T_\phi\).

Usage

gof_auxiliary(
  event_log,
  model,
  auxiliary,
  n_sim = 1000,
  scope = "all",
  mode = "one",
  half_life = NULL,
  seed = NULL,
  n_samples = 1
)

Arguments

event_log

Dyadic event log.

model

Named character vector of <stat> = "linear" mapping for the fitted covariates (must not contain auxiliary).

auxiliary

Name of the statistic to test as an unmodelled feature; must be a statistic computable by endogenous_features().

n_sim

Number of Monte Carlo replicates (default 1000).

scope, mode, half_life, seed

See compare_models().

n_samples

Number of control samples (default 1). With n_samples > 1 the test is run on n_samples case-control samples, drawn with seeds seed, seed + 1, ..., seed + n_samples - 1 (or independently from the current random stream when seed is NULL), and the p-values are combined with the Cauchy combination; see Several control samples.

Value

List with statistic (\(T_\phi\)), p_value, G, u, auxiliary and n_sim. With n_samples > 1, p_value is the Cauchy-combined p-value, p_values holds the per-sample p-values and n_samples their number; the other fields are those of the first sample (seed seed). With n_samples = 1 the result is the single-sample result, without p_values or n_samples.

Several control samples

The test is computed on one case-control sample, so its p-value depends on which controls were drawn. With n_samples \(= S > 1\) the p-values \(p_1, \dots, p_S\) of the same test on \(S\) control samples are combined as $$T = \frac{1}{S}\sum_{s=1}^S \tan\{\pi(1/2 - p_s)\}, \qquad p = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{\arctan T}{\pi}$$ (Liu & Xie 2020), the rule gof_global() uses across covariates. The samples share the events, so the \(p_s\) are dependent. The Cauchy combination is valid under arbitrary dependence among the \(p_s\): when each \(p_s\) is uniform under the null, the tail of \(T\) is asymptotically standard Cauchy whatever their dependence (Liu & Xie 2020, Theorem 1), so \(p\) controls the size at small levels; with identical samples it returns their common p-value. Each \(p_s\) is clamped to \([10^{-15}, 1 - 10^{-15}]\) so that the tangent stays finite. The Monte Carlo p-values of gof_multivariate() and gof_auxiliary() are first floored at \(1/(n_{sim} + 1)\) (p_values keeps the unfloored values). Since \(T\) is at most \(\max_s \tan\{\pi(1/2 - p_s)\}\), the combined p-value is then at least \(1/(n_{sim} + 1)\): a combined p-value equal to that bound means \(p < 1/n_{sim}\) in every sample, and a smaller p-value needs a larger n_sim. The Kolmogorov p-values of gof_univariate() and gof_global() are analytic and are not floored.

References

Boschi M, Wit EC (2025). Goodness of fit in relational event models. Statistics and Computing 36(4).

Liu Y, Xie J (2020). Cauchy combination test: a powerful test with analytic p-value calculation under arbitrary dependency structures. Journal of the American Statistical Association 115(529), 393–402. doi:10.1080/01621459.2018.1554485 .

Examples

data(simulated_events)
gof_auxiliary(simulated_events,
  model = c(reciprocity_count = "linear"),
  auxiliary = "transitivity_count", n_sim = 200, seed = 1)[c("statistic", "p_value")]
#> $statistic
#> [1] 1.775988
#> 
#> $p_value
#> [1] 0.08
#>
